payload.excerpt: How a wedding photo app gathers your guests' photos and videos in one private album, the main types of tool, what to check before you choose, privacy and who owns guest photos, and how to make it work at a destination wedding.
key_takeaways: A wedding photo app collects your guests' candid photos and videos in one private album, alongside your professional photographer's gallery rather than instead of it.

Check any option for its total cost and what is included, browser uploads with no install, full resolution, video, moderation, a full download at the end, how long photos are kept and offline uploads.
Ask guests before their photos are shared publicly, check with parents before sharing images of children, and remove any photo a guest asks you to take down.
At a destination wedding, ask the venue about Wi-Fi and data early, and choose a set-up that lets guests upload later from home.

faq.q: What is the easiest way to collect wedding photos from guests?
faq.a: A shared album with a QR code on every table and a link on your wedding website, mentioned again at the reception and left open for a few weeks afterwards.

faq.q: Do guests need to download an app to share wedding photos?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Look for a tool that lets guests upload from the phone's browser after scanning a QR code, with nothing to install.

faq.q: Can guests upload videos as well as photos?
faq.a: It depends on the tool, so check before you commit that video is supported, kept in original quality and not cut short.

faq.q: Who owns the photos guests take at a wedding?
faq.a: As general information as at November 2026, the Copyright Act's default rule is that the author of a work owns its copyright, which for a photo is generally the person who took it. Ask a guest before you reuse their photo, and check your photographer's contract for your professional images.

faq.q: How do you share a QR code for wedding photos?
faq.a: Print it on table cards and an entrance sign, add it to your website and invitation, and have the MC mention it.

faq.q: Is a disposable camera app a good idea for a wedding?
faq.a: It can be, for a playful mood. Limited shots and a delayed reveal make guests choose their moments, though you will receive fewer photos.
